provenance: Every fixture is a synthetic reconstruction written by hand on made-up content (a shop, a billing script, a web page). None is a verbatim reply from any run.

fixtures.name: valid_array
fixtures.note: Valid control: three intact findings. Repair must leave it unchanged.

fixtures.name: valid_tricky_strings
fixtures.note: Valid control whose strings hold //, /* */, apostrophes, braces and ,] . Repair must not touch text inside a string.

fixtures.name: trailing_comma_in_element
fixtures.note: A comma after the last key of the middle finding.

fixtures.name: trailing_comma_lone_object
fixtures.note: A single finding object with a comma after its last key.

fixtures.name: single_quotes_in_element
fixtures.note: The middle finding uses single quotes for every key and value.

fixtures.name: single_quotes_escapes_lone_object
fixtures.note: Single-quoted strings holding an escaped \' and a bare double quote, which must come out as \".

fixtures.name: line_comment_in_element
fixtures.note: // comments after a value and on a line of their own inside the middle finding. The next finding has // inside a URL string.

fixtures.name: block_comment_in_element
fixtures.note: /* */ comments after a value and between a key and its value inside the middle finding.

fixtures.name: unquoted_keys_in_element
fixtures.note: The middle finding has bare identifier keys.

fixtures.name: mismatched_closer_in_element
fixtures.note: The middle finding closes with ] instead of }.

fixtures.name: extra_closer_in_element
fixtures.note: The middle finding closes with }} .

fixtures.name: mixed_defects_in_element
fixtures.note: One finding with unquoted keys, single quotes, a line comment, a block comment and a trailing comma together.

fixtures.name: missing_closer_array
fixtures.note: Three complete findings; the array's ] is missing. Every element is complete, so all three are kept.

fixtures.name: missing_closer_wrapper
fixtures.note: A {"findings":[...]} wrapper whose array is closed but whose outer } is missing.

fixtures.name: cut_off_open_string
fixtures.note: The reply stops inside a string of the third finding. The open string is never closed, so the third finding stays dropped.

fixtures.name: cut_off_after_value
fixtures.note: The reply stops after a complete value of the third finding, with no open string. The element is cut off by end of input, so it stays dropped.

fixtures.name: cut_off_lone_object
fixtures.note: A lone finding object cut off after a complete value. It is never closed, so nothing is decoded.

fixtures.name: valid_fenced
fixtures.note: Valid control: a fenced verdict after a line of prose.

fixtures.name: valid_tricky_strings
fixtures.note: Valid control whose reasoning holds a URL, an apostrophe, ,} and /* */ . Repair must not touch text inside a string.

fixtures.name: trailing_comma
fixtures.note: A comma after the reasoning value, in a fence after prose.

fixtures.name: single_quotes
fixtures.note: Single quotes for both keys and values; no brace or apostrophe inside a string, so extraction still finds the object.

fixtures.name: line_comment
fixtures.note: A // comment after the verdict value.

fixtures.name: block_comment
fixtures.note: A /* */ comment between the verdict key and its value.

fixtures.name: unquoted_keys
fixtures.note: Bare identifier keys, after a line of prose.

fixtures.name: cut_off
fixtures.note: The reply stops inside the reasoning string. No verdict is taken from it.
